title: Priv EKS Control Plane: Canary Telemetry Adapter Terraform Module
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions an EKS control-plane bootstrap with an integrated 'canary telemetry adapter'. The adapter is a set of auxiliary resources (canary control-plane instances, probe lambdas, and telemetry exporters) that attach to the newly provisioned control plane to validate upgrades, exercise API-server behaviour under controlled traffic, and emit health metrics into our observability pipeline. This module bridges existing priv-vpc bootstrap patterns with explicit canary + telemetry primitives so upgrades and automated repairs can be validated before routing tenant traffic to a control plane. Target users: platform engineers provisioning Redwood Private control planes in customer VPCs.
background: We've had recurring issues where control-plane upgrades (k8s version, control plane autoscaler or cert rotation) introduce subtle API regressions that are only discovered after customers are migrated. Current provisioning modules create control planes but lack a standard canary harness that: 1) traffic-tests API endpoints, 2) validates kube-apiserver metrics and latencies, and 3) surfaces regression signals to Console. This ticket implements an opinionated terraform module that codifies those checks into the provisioning flow.
acceptance_criteria: New terraform module `redwood_priv_eks_controlplane_canary` is published to our terraform registry and versioned
When `canary_mode=true`, module provisions isolated canary control-plane instances (non-customer-traffic) with IAM roles scoped only to probe operations

Module deploys probe lambdas (or Fargate tasks) that run a configurable probe suite (create/delete namespace, API list/watch, auth token rotation) and emit Prometheus-formatted metrics to our telemetry pipeline
Probe results are recorded to CloudWatch metrics and forwarded to Console with labels for control-plane-version and cluster-id
Module provides an upgrade hook integration: terraform apply reports a synthetic health_check boolean that can be used by higher-level orchestrators to gate rollout
Documentation (README + runbook) exists with examples for: fresh bootstraps, upgrade-canary, and canary teardown
E2E smoke tests in CI verify module can create/destroy resources in a sandbox AWS account and that probes produce metrics for at least two consecutive windows
implementation_notes: Prefer minimal infra: use lightweight Fargate tasks over long-lived EC2 where possible to avoid cross-account permissions
Probe suite should be idempotent and safe to run concurrently; avoid destructive operations on tenant namespaces
Telemetry exporter will push to our internal prometheus remote_write endpoint via an IAM role + signed requests
Use Terraform 1.5 practices and module composition (inputs/outputs) compatible with our other priv modules
Expose an output `canary_status` (string) and `canary_metrics_endpoint` (string) for operators to hook into orchestration
IAM roles scoped: only `eks:DescribeCluster`, `eks:ListUpdates`, and limited `sts:AssumeRole` to service tasks
Module should be network-aware: deploy probe tasks into the same private subnets and honor customer VPC NAT egress restrictions when present
tasks: Draft module interface (inputs/outputs) and commit initial skeleton
Prototype probe task (Go Python binary) and local e2e harness
Implement terraform resources: canary control-plane placeholders, probe task, iam roles, metrics exporter config
Add upgrade hook output and terraform `null_resource` local-exec test glue for CI
Write README and runbook with example upgrades and failure remediation
Create CI job to run sandbox apply/destroy and validate metrics emission
Open RFC/Confluence page and request review from SRE and Security
Ship initial 0.1.0 release to internal registry and announce in #platform
test_plan: Unit test: terraform fmt/validate, module unit tests with terratest where feasible
Integration: run terraform apply in sandbox account -> ensure canary tasks start and emit metrics
Upgrade simulation: simulate control-plane version bump and confirm probes detect degraded API surface
Chaos: sporadic latency injection in sandbox to validate probe sensitivity and alerts
Rollback validation: ensure `canary_status` reflects failures and CI can abort higher-level rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 1: land module in infra-modules repo, run canary in sandbox; Stage 2: enable canary_mode for non-critical internal clusters for 2 weeks; Stage 3: enable for select customer migrations behind feature flag; Stage 4: default to on for all private bootstraps after 90% signal quality. Gate each stage with metrics SLOs and a postmortem review if any canary detects a regression.
